balanceSheet.title: Balance sheet
balanceSheet.content:
Shareholders' equity is assets less liabilities; plotted against total liabilities to show leverage.

For NVIDIA Corporation: equity that grows only through revaluations or share issues is not the same as retained earnings.

What to watch:

  • Liabilities growing faster than equity
  • Goodwill share of equity after acquisitions

cashDebt.title: Cash and debt
cashDebt.content:
Cash & equivalents against total borrowings (leases excluded unless noted).

For NVIDIA Corporation: the DCF's net-debt bridge uses these balances at the latest balance-sheet date.

What to watch:

  • Net debt trend versus EBITDA
  • Refinancing dates and covenants in the filings

ebitda.title: EBITDA
ebitda.content:
EBITDA is earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortisation -- an operating-cash proxy that ignores capital intensity.

For NVIDIA Corporation: read it beside CapEx: a business that must reinvest most of its EBITDA is not as cash-generative as the margin suggests.

What to watch:

  • EBITDA margin trend
  • Gap between EBITDA and operating cash flow (working capital)

epsDps.title: EPS and dividends
epsDps.content:
EPS is net income per share; DPS is the cash dividend paid per share. Both are in major currency units.

For NVIDIA Corporation: the payout ratio (DPS / EPS) shows how much of earnings is returned versus reinvested.

What to watch:

  • EPS growth versus net income growth (dilution)
  • Dividends funded from earnings, not debt

fcf.title: Free cash flow
fcf.content:
Reported FCF is operating cash flow less capital expenditure. Owner FCF (from the DCF) further deducts stock-based compensation, interest income and lease principal -- the cash an owner could actually take out.

For NVIDIA Corporation: the gap between net income and owner FCF is the earnings-quality question the valuation is built on.

What to watch:

  • FCF persistently below net income
  • Working-capital swings inflating one year's FCF

margins.title: Margins
margins.content:
Gross margin is revenue less cost of revenue; operating margin deducts operating expenses; net margin is after interest and tax.

For NVIDIA Corporation: the spread between gross and operating margin is the cost of running the business; a widening spread with flat gross margin means opex is growing faster than sales.

What to watch:

  • Direction of operating margin over several years, not one
  • One-offs (impairments, disposals) that distort net margin

ocfCapex.title: Operating cash flow and CapEx
ocfCapex.content:
Operating cash flow is cash generated by operations; CapEx is cash invested in fixed and intangible assets.

For NVIDIA Corporation: CapEx here is shown as stored (sign convention varies by ticker); the DCF splits it into stay-in-business and growth where disclosed.

What to watch:

  • CapEx rising faster than revenue
  • OCF that diverges from EBITDA

profit.title: Profit lines
profit.content:
Gross profit is revenue less cost of revenue; operating income deducts operating expenses; net income is after interest, tax and one-offs.

For NVIDIA Corporation: the three lines together show where margin is made and lost between the top line and the bottom.

What to watch:

  • Operating income growing slower than gross profit (opex creep)
  • Net income far from operating income (interest, tax, one-offs)

revenue.title: Revenue
revenue.content:
Revenue is the top line: what customers paid for goods and services in the period, before any costs.

For NVIDIA Corporation: the growth rate matters more than the level; compare it with the DCF's base-case growth path below.

What to watch:

  • Acceleration or deceleration in YoY growth
  • Whether growth is organic or acquired
  • Interim rows show seasonality

sbc.title: Stock-based compensation and share count
sbc.content:
Stock-based comp is the expense of equity awards; shares outstanding shows the dilution it causes net of buybacks.

For NVIDIA Corporation: the DCF charges SBC as a cash cost and holds the share count flat, so this chart is the check on that assumption.

What to watch:

  • Share count rising while buybacks are advertised
  • SBC as a percentage of revenue

platform.title: Revenue by market platform
platform.content:
Revenue split into NVIDIA's market platforms. Shown as grouped bars (log scale optional), not stacked.

For NVIDIA: Data Center overtook Gaming in FY2021 and now dominates revenue. From FY2027 NVIDIA stopped printing Gaming, ProViz and Automotive, so those series end at FY2026 / Q3 2026 and only Data Center continues to Q2 2027. Early years are restated to the current platform definitions where available.

What to watch:

  • Data Center share of total revenue
  • Gaming as the cyclical, consumer-driven counterweight
  • Automotive ramp from a small base

dcSplit.title: Data Center compute vs networking
dcSplit.content:
Data Center revenue split into GPU/CPU compute and networking (InfiniBand, Spectrum-X Ethernet, NVLink).

For NVIDIA: Disclosed only from FY2023. Networking attach rate shows whether NVIDIA is selling full rack-scale systems rather than chips alone.

What to watch:

  • Networking growing faster than compute (system-level lock-in)
  • Compute lumpiness around product transitions (Hopper to Blackwell to Rubin)

segments.title: Reportable segments
segments.content:
Compute & Networking versus Graphics, the two reportable segments, with segment operating income.

For NVIDIA: Compute & Networking contains Data Center and Automotive; Graphics contains Gaming and ProViz. Segment income excludes the unallocated 'All Other' (SBC, acquisition costs, the FY2023 Arm charge), so it exceeds consolidated operating income.

What to watch:

  • Compute & Networking margin versus Graphics margin
  • Graphics income stability through the gaming cycle

opex.title: Operating leverage
opex.content:
R&D, SG&A and total operating expenses as a percentage of revenue.

For NVIDIA: FY2023 opex includes the $1.35B Arm termination charge, which lifts that year's ratio. Since FY2024 revenue has grown far faster than opex, so the ratio has collapsed and operating margin has risen.

What to watch:

  • Whether opex % stabilises as revenue growth slows
  • R&D intensity: cutting it to flatter margin would be a warning
  • SBC embedded in both lines

liquidity.title: Liquidity
liquidity.content:
Cash & equivalents plus short-term investments against total debt. The chart shows them as separate bars; add the first two for total liquidity.

For NVIDIA: The $25B June 2026 note issue took total debt from $8.5B to $33.4B, so debt now matters for the first time in years, though liquidity remains far larger. The DCF net-debt bridge uses these balances.

What to watch:

  • Debt use of proceeds: buybacks, supply commitments or acquisitions
  • Cash plus investments versus purchase commitments
  • Interest cost against the interest income already excluded from Owner FCF
